slides.headline: Big bushwalk, wobbly legs the next day?
slides.sub: Where massage helps hikers recover, and where it doesn't.

slides.title: Downhill is the hard part
slides.body: Walking downhill asks your quads and calves to brake with every step. That's why soreness is often worst after the descent, especially on long stair sections like those on Sydney's coastal walks.

slides.title: Where massage can help
slides.body: A remedial massage a day or two later can ease tightness in the calves, quads, hips and feet and help you move more comfortably. Research suggests it mainly helps how sore you feel.

slides.title: What massage won't do
slides.body: It won't make up for a big jump in distance or elevation. Training on hills and stairs in the weeks beforehand usually does more to reduce next-day soreness than anything afterwards.

slides.title: Recovery on the day
slides.body: Drink plenty of water, especially in summer heat, eat a decent meal and take an easy walk the next morning. Sitting still for hours on the drive home often leaves legs stiffer.

slides.title: When it's not just sore legs
slides.body: Sharp pain in one spot, swelling in a calf, pain that worsens rather than eases after a few days, or a knee or ankle that won't take weight needs a physio or GP check.

slides.headline: Legs need some recovery work?
slides.body: Our remedial massage therapists at Hybrid Physiotherapy focus on calves, quads, hips and feet, and suggest ways to prepare for your next walk. Book online, link in bio.

caption:
Great day on the track, then the stairs at home feel impossible? That's your quads after all those downhills.

Descending asks your legs to brake with every step, which is why soreness often peaks a day or two after a big bushwalk. A remedial massage can ease tightness and help you move more comfortably, though research suggests it mainly helps how sore you feel.

The bigger win is preparation. Hills and stairs in the weeks before a long walk usually do more than anything afterwards.

Calf swelling or pain that keeps getting worse is worth a GP or physio check.
